sections.title: The Superiority of the New Covenant
observations: In this section, the author of Hebrews emphasizes the superiority of the new covenant established by Christ over the old covenant. The old covenant, given through Moses, was a shadow of the good things to come, while the new covenant is the fulfillment of God's promises.

The high priestly ministry of Jesus is highlighted, showing that He serves in the true tabernacle in heaven, not in a man-made structure. This underscores the divine origin and eternal nature of His priesthood.

sections.title: The Promise of a New Covenant
observations: The author quotes from Jeremiah 31:31-34 to illustrate God's promise of a new covenant. This new covenant is characterized by an internal transformation where God's laws are written on the hearts of His people, signifying a personal relationship with Him.
The new covenant also emphasizes forgiveness of sins, which is a central theme in the work of Christ. This marks a significant shift from the old covenant, which required continual sacrifices.

importantVerses.commentary: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, inasmuch as He is also Mediator of a better covenant, which was established on better promises.
For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more.

questions: What does it mean for Jesus to be the Mediator of a better covenant?
How does the new covenant fulfill the promises made in the Old Testament?
In what ways does the internal transformation of believers under the new covenant differ from the external observance of the law in the old covenant?
